credits.desc: box kalimba: thumb-plucked steel tines, bell-like 6.3x overtone, wooden box glow
West African balafon: rough-tuned bars over gourds with buzzing spider-silk mirlitons
cicada drone: tymbal click buzz in a resonant band centred on the pitch; swells and sags away
bass marimba with big soft mallets: deep breathing resonator hum
tree-frog choir on one note: five frogs, rattling pitched croaks in loose overlapping rhythms
caxixi: woven basket of seeds, soft wicker swish then a hard gourd chick
orchestral glockenspiel: brass mallets on steel bars, piercing sparkling ring
handpan: finger-struck steel dome, tuned octave and fifth blooming out of the note
bamboo dizi: bright, reedy buzz from the dimo membrane, quick ornamental scoops
Warm string section: eight detuned players, slow swelling attack, independent vibratos, wide stereo
Sundanese angklung: octave bamboo tubes rattled in their frame for the gate length
mbira dzavadzimu in a deze gourd: wide keys, sizzling shell-and-bottle-cap rattles
stopped-cane pan pipes: hollow odd-harmonic tone, big breathy "puh" chiff, late slow vibrato
rainstick: pebbles trickle through cactus spines for the gate length
bullfrog "jug-o-rum": rough low pulsing croak with a booming vocal-sac resonance
temple blocks (mokugyo): round carved hollow skulls, warm pitched knock
claves: two rosewood sticks, a pure ringing click over cupped hands
Fretless bass: singing mwah, slides up into each note, slow delayed vibrato
marimba with hard plastic mallets: bright knocking attack, ringing 4th partial
field cricket: pure pitched chirps of four pulses, repeating while the note is held
concert rosewood marimba, cord mallets: warm tube bloom, woody tock
toucan / hornbill clack: hollow double bill-snap with a tuned wooden knock
marimba with soft yarn mallets: round, almost flute-like, no click
orchestral xylophone: hard mallets, quint-tuned bars, dry bright crack
celesta: felt hammers on steel plates over wooden resonators, sugar-plum glow
glass harp: wet fingers circling water-tuned glasses, crystalline sustained voice
water-tuned wine glasses tapped with a spoon: pure ping with a wet wobble
music-box comb: pin-plucked steel teeth, tiny tick, glassy shimmer in a wood case
Five-string banjo: metal-fingerpick snap and a ringing drum-head body that twangs then dies fast
Brazilian cavaquinho: steel-strung chorinho brightness, crisp pick, quick shimmering decay
Andean charango: sparkly nylon courses, the middle course doubled an octave down, tiny bright body
Hammered dulcimer: wooden hammers on courses of three wires, shimmering unison beating, long sustain
Concert pedal harp: round finger pluck near mid-string (hollow, odd-harmonic), long glowing soundboard ring
Wire-strung clarsach: fingernail-plucked brass strings, bell-like and endlessly ringing
Japanese koto: ivory tsume twang near the bridge, nasal paulownia body, plucked string settling in pitch
Bright paired-course mandolin; holds of more than 0.3 s become a shimmering down-up tremolo, the classic Oldfield sound
Clean single-coil electric: glassy pickup resonance, a breath of valve warmth, muted at gate end
gibbon whoop: pure hooting voice swooping up a huge interval into the note, wild vibrato
Oldfield sustain lead: singing fuzz with infinite-feeling sustain, slight scoop, slow wide delayed vibrato and blooming feedback
Celesta: felt hammers on steel bars over wooden resonators, sugar-plum soft shimmer
Clavinet: rubber-tip struck string, funky two-pickup quack, yarn-damped staccato
Reed electric piano: nasal steel-reed tone that barks and growls under a heavy hand
Suitcase tine piano: mellow bell tone swimming in stereo auto-pan tremolo
Tine electric piano: bell-like ping, round body, pickup bark when struck hard
Concert grand: stiff inharmonic strings, felt hammers that brighten with force, unison beating, soundboard thump
Harpsichord: 8+4 quill-plucked choirs, brilliant and metallic, jack-return click on release
Honky-tonk saloon piano: badly detuned unisons warbling against each other, hard worn hammers
Mellotron tape flute: breathy, wavering, nostalgic tape flute with recorded vibrato
Upright parlour piano: shorter, more inharmonic strings, boxy cabinet, a woody knock and quicker fade
Musette accordion: three reeds detuned wet, shimmering Parisian beat, bellows swells
Bandoneon: octave-paired reeds, dark woody tango melancholy, expressive slow swell
English concertina: single sweet reed per button, quick crisp speech, small hexagonal box
Tonewheel organ 888000000: key click, 3rd-harmonic percussion, warm tube drive, slow Leslie chorale
Full-drawbar screaming organ through an overdriven Leslie on fast
Soft gospel/ballad registration 008800000 with slow Leslie: hollow and breathy
Farfisa combo organ: thin reedy pulse waves, bright and buzzy with fast vibrato
howler-monkey roar: growling swell from "oo" to "aa" through a huge hyoid resonance
Hand-pumped harmonium: two reeds a hair apart, bright nasal buzz, bellows breathing
Lowrey-style home organ: mellow divider flute tabs 16+8+4, lush vibrato, gentle glide into notes, slow rotor
Melodica: mouth-blown single reed, hollow nasal honk with breath and a wavering tongue attack
Church pipe organ: principal 8, flute 8 and octave 4, chiffing speech and wind, rank beating
Chiffy stopped flute 8 + open flute 4 with tremulant: woody, breathy chamber organ
Full organ plenum: 16 bourdon to mixture and trumpet, majestic cathedral grandeur
Victorian pump reed organ: soft 8+4 reeds, slow wheezy speech, vox-humana fan tremolo
bansuri: deep, breathy bamboo; slow meend glide up into the note, late singing vibrato
silver concert flute: clean breathy edge tone, flute vibrato that blooms in amplitude and pitch
flageolet: sweet sponge-chamber whistle, gentle, slightly veiled, light vibrato
clay vessel ocarina: almost pure, round and hooty, gentle chiff, soft vibrato
Andean quena: notched-edge attack with a sforzando puff, wide fast vibrato, wild breath
alto recorder: woody, plain, nearly vibrato-free; soft "du" tongued fipple chiff
shakuhachi: muraiki breath explosion, meri scoop from below, deep yuri vibrato, atari fall-off
oboe: nasal, plaintive double reed with strong bright formants and a quick, tight vibrato
soprano sax: bright conical reed, airy subtone at soft, singing developing vibrato
uilleann pipes chanter: sweet, reedy, intimate; crisp tight staccato and a subtle cran flick
open trumpet: brilliant lip-buzz with a fast brassy blat at forte and a slight late vibrato
harmon-muted trumpet: thin, buzzy, intimate nasal whine with a sultry late vibrato
Erhu: nasal python-skin fiddle, slides into each note, wide expressive finger vibrato
Irish fiddle: rosiny short-bow attack, bright and dry, only a hint of late vibrato
Viola: husky alto bowing, darker body, veiled and warm
Solo violin: bright bowed Helmholtz tone through a resonant maple body, singing delayed vibrato
Pizzicato section: five players plucking slightly apart, soft woody pops
Tremolo strings: a section bowing rapid unsynchronised strokes, nervous rustling shimmer
8-bit pulse lead: duty switching, 4-bit volume steps, stepped vibrato
DX7-style electric bell: glassy tine ding over a mellowing FM body
FM glass marimba: short crystalline mallet tone with a glassy 1:4 attack
pulsar beacon: a pitch-dropping "pew" blip repeated three times into the distance
satellite ping: ring-modulated metallic blip bouncing in a ping-pong echo
theremin: eerie near-sine with slow-hand portamento and a wide singing vibrato
Trinidad tenor (lead) steel pan: bright singing note, octave swirling in and out
double-second steel pan: warmer, rounder alto pan with a sympathetic skirt ring
vibraphone, motor on: aluminium bars, rotating resonator discs, damper pedal
vibraphone, motor off, cord mallets: cool glassy bell-tone with a soft ping
songbird trill: flick up, then a sparkling in-key trill on the note and the tone above
Spanish classical guitar: warm flesh-and-nail pluck, 100/200/400 Hz cedar-top body bloom
Double-bass pizzicato: big woody plunk, tension pitch-drop at the attack, fast-fading gut tone
Irish tin whistle: bright, pure-and-piercing fipple tone, instant attack for cuts and rolls
Cello: rich woody bowing with a resonant low body, broad slow vibrato
marimba de chonta: palm-wood bars over guadua bamboo tubes, hollow warbling bonk
bamboo stamping tube: hollow air-column pop with a ground thud and bamboo clack
Ghanaian gyil: dry hardwood keys, heavy nasal gourd buzz on every note
giant hollowed-log slit drum (garamut): booming cavity, thudding lip strike
tuned slit drum: knocking wood tongues over a resonant box
small hardwood tongue drum: sweet hollow tok with a box breath
wooden agung: hollow log played like a gong, padded beater, humming bloom
bonang: bossed bronze kettle-gong pots on cords, round singing ping
gamelan gender pair: thin bronze keys over bamboo tubes, padded mallets, slow ombak
gong ageng: huge bossed gong, slow breathing ombak, shimmer blooms and sags in pitch
kempul: hanging bossed gong, padded beater, deep beating ombak swell
Chinese opera gong (xiaoluo): flat bronze, the pitch whoops upward after the hit
large opera gong (daluo): crashing bronze that sags downward in pitch
gamelan saron pair: thick bronze keys, horn mallet clang, shimmering ombak beats
orchestral tam-tam: dark hum that blooms into a roaring metallic shimmer
bowed waterphone: steel rods over a sloshing resonator, eerie bending howls
bell tree: a beater slides down nested brass bells, descending sparkle
bronze church bell: hum, prime, minor-third tierce and nominal, iron clapper clang
antique cymbals: thick tuned brass discs, pure endless shimmer
mark-tree chimes: a finger sweep through rods, upward glittering cascade
Tibetan singing bowl: struck, then rubbed with the stick - swelling wah-wah drone
"plus... tubular bells": the chime hit with a hammer, harsh steel clang, wide stereo
Arabic oud: fretless paired gut courses, feather-risha attack, deep dark bowl-back thump
Sitar-ish: jawari buzz with a sweeping formant and a halo of sympathetic taraf strings
Soprano ukulele: soft nylon thumb-pluck, short plinky decay, small sweet box
Crunchy humbucker rhythm guitar: bridge-pickup bite into a cranked 2x12, tight palm-muted end
12-string acoustic: octave courses struck first, chorusing jangle spread across the stereo field
Pick-played bass: clicky plectrum attack, bridge-pickup growl, punchy mids
Double bass arco: growling rosin-heavy bow, deep boxy body, slow bloom
Music box: pinned steel comb teeth, tinkling inharmonic ping with paired-tooth beating
nose flute: soft hollow nasal hoot, wavering unsteady pitch, low airy hiss
sopranino recorder: tiny, piping, squeaky-bright tongued attack
tin whistle with a built-in "cut" grace note flicked above each attack (Irish ornament)
bassoon: dark buzzing double reed, woody 500 Hz formant, comic in staccato, noble when held
clarinet: hollow odd-harmonic chalumeau, warming to brighter clarion when pushed; straight tone
Armenian duduk: dark, velvety, breath-heavy wide reed; scoops from below, sobbing slow vibrato
harmonica: buzzy free reed, cupped-hand wah opening, bluesy draw-bend from below, hand tremolo
Highland bagpipe chanter: blaring, piercing, constant-pressure reed with a gracenote snap
Highland drones: two beating tenor drones + bass drone an octave down, striking in with a gurgle
uilleann drones: sweet humming bass, baritone and tenor drones in octaves (pitch = bass drone)
uilleann regulators: wrist-struck root-fifth-octave reed chords, crisp and sweet
alphorn: long wooden natural horn, soft pure overtones blooming slowly, mountain-wide
conch shell horn: hollow ritual blare, breathy and wavering, sagging off the end of the note
French horn: warm, round, hand-in-bell darkness; noble swell and bloom at forte
tenor trombone: slide scoop into the note, broad buzzing brass that brightens hard with force
tuba: huge, soft-edged, dark bass brass with a puffed lip attack
children's choir: pure straight-toned 'ah-oh', light and airy, small bright formants
choir on "ooh": soft, dark, hollow; slow swell, gentle vibrato
humming choir "mmm": closed-mouth, warm, intimate, soft buzzing nasal glow
low male "om" chant: three monks, "oh" closing to "oo" and a buzzing hum
robot formant voice: rigid buzz, vowels jumping in steps, speech-chip aliasing sparkle
solo soprano vocalise: ringing "ah" turning to "oh", operatic vibrato that blooms
overtone throat singing: pressed drone whose harmonics whistle a stepping melody
whispered breath choir: ghostly vowel-shaped air, faintly tinted with the note
bat sonar: constant-pitch calls with FM drop-offs, accelerating into a feeding buzz
stridulating beetle: rhythmic bursts of hard little resonant ticks (pitch tunes the body)
tuned bird whistle: clean glide up into the note, shy vibrato, a flick down as it lets go
pulsing cicada: the same tymbal buzz phrased in 4 Hz throbs
coquí two-tone "co-QUÍ": a fifth below, then a rising chirp onto the top note (pitch)
hummingbird hover: buzzing wing hum on the note, flickering wingbeat air, darting wobble
monkey chatter: squeaky excited "chk-eek" syllables on the note with in-key leaps
owl "hoo... hoooo": soft breathy hoots, the long one held on the note and sinking away
parrot squawk: chaotic, harsh beaky screech arching in pitch (pitch is a tint)
acid 303 bass: squelchy resonant saw; accent opens the sweep and the resonance
analog synth brass: detuned saw stack whose filter blares open, 80s fanfare
8-bit triangle bass: NES staircase triangle with a little pluck
Moog-style lead: fat detuned saws + sub through a driven ladder filter that sweeps down
wavetable nebula pad: spectrum morphing odd->full while a resonant band scans the harmonics
noise riser: resonant noise band and ghost tone sweeping up three octaves over the gate
supersaw pad: seven detuned saws spread wide, slow filter bloom, long release
vocoder choir pad: detuned saw carrier through vowel-shaped bands, "ah" to "oh"
warm analog pad: slow PWM oscillators an octave apart, soft and chorused
orchestral gran cassa: huge soft beater, deep rolling boom; thunder roll when held
bodhran with hand pressed behind the skin: higher, tight, clipped
bongo: small tight heads, crisp high ring under the fingertips
cajon bass: palm on the plywood face, box boom and faint snare
cajon slap: fingers at the top corner, cracking plate and sizzling wires
conga muffled tone: palm stays on the head, dark short thump
conga open tone: singing rawhide note over a tall staved shell
conga slap: closed, popping crack with a choked ring
large frame drum (tar): soft fingers, deep centre dum, long low ring
modern produced kick: pitch-swept thump, beater click, saturated
brushed snare: wire-brush tap and circular swish for the gate length
tabla bayan: deep ghe stroke, the heel slides and the pitch swoops up
tabla dayan: the black syahi makes the head ring with true harmonics (tin stroke)
talking drum, struck squeezed: the note sighs downward as the cords relax
kit tom: stick on a double-headed tom, punchy pitch drop and shell ring
concert toms with felt mallets: round, tuned, ritual; rolls when held
udu struck on the belly with fingers: clay ring over a soft air hum
water drum: half calabash floating in a basin, wobbling liquid dum
agogo low bell: hand-forged iron cone, stick-struck clank
cabasa: steel bead chains twisted on a ridged cylinder, tight chk
cowbell: flat sheet-iron bell, two clanging modes, hand-muted
crash cymbal: big bloom of noise through a dense metal cloud
ride cymbal: stick ping on the bow, a long glassy wash
suspended cymbal swell: soft-mallet roll growing for the gate
finger cymbals (zills): two little brass cups kissed rim to rim
guiro: stick scraped along a ridged gourd for the gate length
hand claps: a few people clapping together in a small room
seed-pod rattle shaken for the gate length: clacky woody seeds
egg shaker: plastic shell, fine beads, one crisp shake
shekere: bead net slapped against a big gourd, rattling thump
tambourine: jingles clash on a small goatskin frame
triangle: bent steel rod and beater, a long silvery shimmer
woodblock: hollow slotted block, dry hollow tok
agogo high bell: the smaller cone, a fourth above
ganza: metal tube shaker, bright metallic samba hiss
djembe bass: flat palm in the centre, goblet body booms
dundunba: big double-headed cowhide bass drum, stick-struck boom
sangban: middle dunun, round woody bounce
djembe tone: fingers at the edge, ringing round goatskin note
kenkeni: small dunun, tight hard-stick knock that drives the ensemble
djembe slap: whip-crack of loose fingers on tight skin
bodhran: goatskin frame drum and wooden tipper, the Ommadawn heartbeat
udu bloop: palm on the clay pot side-hole, a liquid rising boom
talking drum: hooked-stick strike, the arm squeezes the cords - pitch rises with the gate
didgeridoo: buzzing drone with rhythmic "wow" formant sweeps, tongue-pushed overtone band
African call-and-response leader: strong open chest voice, scooped attack, falls away
African chorus response: many open-throated voices with octave doubling, punchy
West-African kora: bright thumb-plucked harp-lute with calabash boom and sizzling buzzer bridge
Berimbau musical bow: stick-struck wire, coin buzz and gourd wah-wah that pumps for as long as the gate
surdo: deep samba bass, felt mallet on plastic, long open hum
pedal timpani: felt mallet, tuned principal tone over the copper kettle; rolls when held
Fingered electric bass: round two-finger thump, neck-pickup warmth, muted when the gate ends
Oldfield "double-speed" guitar: half-speed-recorded steel string sped up, chipmunk-bright, compressed and glittering
Steel-string dreadnought: crisp pick, booming low end, long silvery sustain
orchestral tubular bells: rawhide strike on the cap, clangorous chime, long hum
mixed choir on "aah": eight singers, each with own vibrato and pitch, warm and wide
acoustic kick with felt beater and blanket: round woof
snare drum: stick on coated head, crisp wire sizzle; buzz roll when held
string machine: Solina-style thin saws in a swirling triple-delay ensemble
granular shimmer: a sparkling cloud of pitched grains on the note, octave and twelfth
sub bass: deep sine with velocity growl and a tiny thump
whale moan: rising into the note, lazy waver, slowly opening throat, sinking glide, echoes
Mellotron tape strings: wobbly three-violin tape replay, dusty bandwidth, runs out after 8 s
Irish bouzouki: long-scale steel courses, low ones in octaves, jangly plectrum drone-strummer
kookaburra laugh: a cackling run of harsh "ha" syllables that builds and tails off

mc.text: Spanish guitar, and introducing acoustic guitar
